questions.stem: Which of the following is an objective of Vendor Risk Management? (Choose two.)

options.text: To help vendors improve their security posture and preparedness
To assess and manage the risk from interactions with vendors and third parties
To help negotiate the best possible price for a product or service from the vendor
To verify that vendors have adequate measures and processes in place to ensure profitability of vendor

questions.explanation: The objectives of Vendor Risk Management are to help vendors improve their security posture and preparedness (A) and to assess and manage the risk from interactions with vendors and third parties (B). VRM is designed to evaluate vendor security and manage third-party risk exposure. Negotiating prices (C) is a procurement function, not a risk management objective. Ensuring vendor profitability (D) is not a risk management goal.

questions.stem: The Vendor records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: Vendor records are stored in the Company [core_company] table (A). ServiceNow VRM uses the core_company table as the foundation for storing vendor/third-party organization data. Department [cmn_department] (B) stores organizational department records. Task [task] (C) is the base task table. User [sys_user] (D) stores individual user accounts, not company/vendor records.

questions.stem: Internal roles include: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The internal roles are Vendor Risk Manager (B), Vendor Risk Assessor (D), and Vendor Risk Reviewer (E). Per the docs: 'designed for users with the following roles: TPR manager [vendor_risk_manager], TPR assessor [vendor_assessor], Third-party assessment reviewer [vendor_assessment_reviewer].' These are the internal organizational roles. Vendor Contact (A) and Primary Vendor Contact (C) are external roles assigned to vendor-side personnel.

questions.stem: Roles preceded by sn_vdr_risk are for which scope?
questions.explanation: Roles preceded by sn_vdr_risk are for the GRC: Vendor Risk Management scope (D). The sn_vdr_risk prefix denotes the Vendor Risk Management scoped application. Per the docs: the Vendor Risk Management plugin contains these role definitions. GRC: Vendor Risk Remediation (A), GRC: Risk Management (C), and GRC: Vendor Risk Core (B) are different scopes with different role prefixes.

questions.stem: Before any changes to the configuration of an application are made, it is recommended that the correct update set and application scope are selected. What role is required for this functionality?

options.text: The Vendor Administrator role is required for this functionality
The Data Administrator role is required for this functionality
The User Administrator role is required for this functionality
The System Administrator role is required for this functionality

questions.explanation: The System Administrator role (D) is required to select the correct update set and application scope before making configuration changes. System Administrators control update set management and application scope switching at the platform level. Vendor Administrator (A), Data Administrator (B), and User Administrator (C) do not have update set management permissions.

questions.stem: What is the definition of ‘Risk Management’?

options.text: Policies/Standards/Procedures established to ensure an organization is aligned with corporate strategy and expectations are clearly defined
The process of conforming to standards, policies, and remediation of audit findings
The elimination of vulnerable surface area in an enterprise environment
Process to identify, assess, and respond to risks, threats and vulnerabilities that could compromise the business

questions.explanation: Risk Management is the process to identify, assess, and respond to risks, threats and vulnerabilities that could compromise the business (D). This definition covers the full risk lifecycle from identification through assessment and response. Policy alignment (A) describes Governance. Conforming to standards (B) describes Compliance. Eliminating vulnerable surface area (C) describes security hardening, not Risk Management.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the main benefit of using the Vendor Portal?

options.text: Assessments are performed via the Vendor Portal and spreadsheets
More efficiently communicating Assessments with a single contact
Assessments are shared through the Vendor Portal and email
More efficiently completing Assessments via the Vendor Portal

questions.explanation: The main benefit of using the Vendor Portal is more efficiently completing assessments via the Vendor Portal (D). The portal provides vendors with a dedicated interface to complete assessment questionnaires, respond to issues, and manage contacts — streamlining the assessment workflow. Spreadsheet use (A) and email sharing (C) are less efficient alternatives the portal replaces. Single contact communication (B) is a secondary benefit.

questions.stem: Baseline email notifications that help to automate the vendor risk management process are installed with which plugin?
questions.explanation: Baseline email notifications that automate the vendor risk management process are installed with the GRC: Vendor Risk Management plugin (A). The Vendor Risk Management application includes pre-configured notification workflows for assessment distribution and status updates. GRC: Audit Management (B), Risk Management (C), and Policy and Compliance Management (D) are separate GRC applications with their own notification sets.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the role assignment of vendor contacts in Vendor Risk Management?

options.text: When vendor contacts are created, they are automatically assigned the snc_internal role and the snc_external role
When vendor contacts are created, they must be manually assigned the snc_external role
When vendor contacts are created, they are automatically assigned the snc_internal role
When vendor contacts are created, they are automatically assigned the snc_external role

questions.explanation: When vendor contacts are created, they are automatically assigned the snc_external role (D). Per the docs: 'It's normal for a contact to have the snc_external role because the vendor_contact role includes it.' This external role grants vendor contacts access to the third-party portal for responding to assessments. They are not assigned snc_internal (C) as they are external users. Manual role assignment (B) is not required for the base external role.

questions.stem: What can a vendor contact do in the Vendor Portal? (Choose four.)

options.text: Communicate or share information with other vendors of the assessing organization
Create new issues and tasks for the vendor risk assessor team
Review and respond to issues created by the assessing organization
Manage vendor contacts and task assignments within the vendor organization
Respond to assessments sent by the assessing organization

questions.explanation: In the Vendor Portal, a vendor contact can update answers to returned questionnaires (A), review and respond to issues created by the assessing organization (D), manage vendor contacts and task assignments within the vendor organization (E), and respond to assessments sent by the assessing organization (F). Communicating with other vendors (B) is not supported. Creating new issues for the assessor team (C) is not a vendor contact capability.

questions.stem: Which functions can be performed in the Vendor Portal? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The functions available in the Vendor Portal are Assessment response (A), Contact Management (B), and Issue remediation (C). The portal enables vendors to complete assessments, manage their contact information, and remediate identified issues. Scheduling web meetings (D) and virtual agent requests (E) are not standard Vendor Portal functions.

questions.stem: Where do vendors manage issues, respond to requests, and fulfill tasks assigned to them?
questions.explanation: Vendors manage issues, respond to requests, and fulfill tasks assigned to them through the Vendor Portal (B). The Vendor Portal is the dedicated interface for vendor-side activities in the TPRM process. Spreadsheets (A) and email (D) are less efficient alternatives. Vendors do not have direct access to the ServiceNow Platform (C) — they use the portal.

questions.stem: Which statements most accurately describe assignments to vendor contacts? (Choose two.)

options.text: Individual sections in the questionnaire or document request can be assigned
A questionnaire or document request cannot be assigned to multiple vendor contacts
A questionnaire can be read by vendor contacts that are not assigned
A questionnaire can only be completed by assigned vendor contacts

questions.explanation: A questionnaire can be read by vendor contacts that are not assigned (C) and can only be completed by assigned vendor contacts (D). This allows read-only visibility for all contacts while restricting response submission to designated assignees. Individual sections cannot be separately assigned (A is false). Questionnaires can be assigned to multiple vendor contacts (B is false).

questions.stem: What are the baseline mandatory fields when creating a new Vendor Contact? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The baseline mandatory fields when creating a new Vendor Contact are Name/First and Last name (A), Vendor (B), and Email (D). Per the docs: 'First name, Last name, Email' are required standard contact information, and the Vendor association is needed to link the contact to their organization. Department (C) and Role (E) are optional fields that can be populated but are not baseline mandatory.

questions.stem: Which of these options can be used in data cleansing when importing vendor data? (Choose three.)

options.text: Data Import or Data Source Transform

questions.explanation: For data cleansing when importing vendor data, you can use Field Normalization Rules (C), Fix Scripts (D), and Data Import or Data Source Transform (E). Field Normalization rules standardize field values; Fix Scripts handle custom data transformations; Data Import/Transform maps source data to target fields. Data Policies (A) enforce field validation but are not data cleansing tools. ACLs (B) control access. UI Policies (F) control form behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following are functions of the Vendor Risk Assessor? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a Primary Contact record for a Vendor

questions.explanation: The Vendor Risk Assessor can access completed assessments from vendors (B), create issues for the vendor (D), and create a Primary Contact record for a Vendor (E). Enabling communications across vendors (A) is not an assessor function — vendors don't communicate with each other through the platform. Updating vendor contract deadlines (C) is not a standard assessor function.

questions.stem: What third-party vendor security evaluation solutions are commonly integrated with VRM out-of-the-box? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Third-party vendor security evaluation solutions integrated out-of-the-box are Bitsight (C) and Security Scorecard (D). Per the docs: ServiceNow TPRM has standard integrations with leading security rating providers. MyScoreMetrics (A) is not a known out-of-the-box integration. Vendor Insights (B) is a ServiceNow product, not a third-party security rating service.

questions.stem: What is the no code option to cleaning data being loaded into the Vendor Risk application?
questions.explanation: The no-code option for cleaning data loaded into the Vendor Risk application is Field Normalization (B). Field Normalization allows administrators to standardize and normalize field values without writing code — configuring rules through a UI interface. Fix Scripts (A) require scripting. Import (C) is the data loading mechanism itself, not a cleansing option.

questions.stem: When will the tiering value appear on the Vendor record?

options.text: When the Tiering Assessment record state is closed
When the Tiering Assessment record state is Tiering Assessment
When all tiering assessments have been completed

questions.explanation: The tiering value appears on the Vendor record when the Tiering Assessment record state is closed (A). Per the docs: 'The risk tier is assigned to the third party when the tiering assessment is closed.' The tiering process: assessment runs → scores averaged → mapped to risk tiers → tier assigned on close. The value does not appear at the Tiering Assessment state (B) or when all tiering assessments are completed (C).

questions.stem: What can be used to automatically assign a Vendor tier value?
questions.explanation: A Tiering Assessment (C) is used to automatically assign a Vendor tier value. Per the docs: the tiering assessment process creates an assessment instance, averages response scores into a tiering score, maps it to risk tiers, and assigns the risk tier to the third party when the assessment is closed. A Risk Assessment (A) measures risk but doesn't automatically tier vendors. A configuration setting (B) is not used for tiering. A Vendor Tiering Rule (D) and Visual Task Board (E) are not standard tiering mechanisms.

questions.stem: If clean data is not provided by the customer, what baseline solutions are available within the platform? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The baseline solutions within the platform are Field Normalization Plugin (B), System Definition Fix Scripts Module (D), and System Import Transform Map Scripts (E). Field Normalization standardizes field values; Fix Scripts handle custom transformations via script; Transform Map Scripts map and cleanse data during import. Integration Hub ETL Plugin (A) is a separate add-on. Service Graph Connector (C) is for CMDB ingestion, not general data cleansing.

questions.stem: On the Contact record, there is a field for the Vendor name. This is which field (with a label change) from the sys_user table?
questions.explanation: The Vendor name field on the Contact record is the 'company' [company] field from the sys_user table with a label change (C). The sys_user table includes a standard 'Company' reference field that links users to their organization. In VRM, this field is relabeled 'Vendor' on the vendor contact form to reflect the third-party context. sn_vendor (A) and vendor_name (D) are not sys_user fields. company_name (B) is not a standard sys_user field.

questions.stem: The Template Designer is leveraged to create which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Template Designer is used to create Document Request Templates (A) and Questionnaire Templates (D). Per the docs: navigation leads to 'Assessment setup > Questionnaire Templates or... Document Request Templates' for creating templates. Assessment Template (B) is a SAE-level record; Vendor Risk Assessment (C) is a runtime assessment instance, not a template. The designer creates the template structures that are later used in assessments.

questions.stem: All Assessment Metrics within a Metric Category are scored, are rolled up, and get a score of.
questions.explanation: Assessment Metrics are scored on a 0-100 scale (B). Per the docs: the scoring formula normalizes responses — '([Highest normalization input value] / [Maximum of normalization input values]) * 100' — producing a 0-100 range. Metric categories aggregate metric scores, also resulting in 0-100. Scales of 0-5 (A), 0-10 (D), or 0-20 (C) are not used in VRM metric scoring.

questions.stem: The Template Designer contains which of the following elements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Option to create an Assessment Template and assign to a vendor
Properties for the supported question data types
Options to weight questions or sections
Design canvas for creating the questions and answers

questions.explanation: The Template Designer contains Properties for supported question data types (B) and the Design canvas for creating questions/answers (D). Per the docs: 'Controls — Supported question data types available in the Controls palette' and 'Categories — New assessment opens in the Design view.' Assigning templates to vendors (A) is done from the assessment record. Weighting questions (C) is configured separately outside the designer canvas.

questions.stem: Where can the score for each Assessment Metric or Metric Category be configured?
questions.explanation: The score for each Assessment Metric or Metric Category is configured on the Assessment Metric Type record (D). The Assessment Metric Type (questionnaire template) contains the scoring configuration including metric weights and category weights. Assessment Metric Category (A) and Assessment Template (B) do not contain the scoring setup. Assessment record (C) is a runtime instance, not a configuration record.

questions.stem: In order to evaluate a vendor on a recurring basis, configure a record in this table:
questions.explanation: To evaluate a vendor on a recurring basis, configure a Repeating Assessments (C) record. Per the docs: 'You can create repeating assessments if you are using the classic assessment engine.' Repeating Assessments is the dedicated module for scheduling recurring vendor evaluations. Repeating Surveys (A) is not a VRM module. Assessment Metric (B) is a single question. Assessment Metric Type (D) is the questionnaire template structure.

questions.stem: A Document Request Template is a record in which table?
questions.explanation: A Document Request Template is a record in the Assessment metric type [asmt_metric_type] table (D). Per the docs: 'Metric type or Assessment metric type: A questionnaire template.' Both questionnaire templates and document request templates are stored in the asmt_metric_type table, differentiated by a type field. Document request item [sn_document_template] (A) is not the correct table. sn_vdr_risk_asmt_assessment (B) stores runtime assessments.

questions.stem: From an Assessment record, the vendor risk assessor can click on “View Responses” to see which of the following?
questions.explanation: Clicking 'View Responses' on an Assessment record shows Assessment Responses (D). This displays the actual vendor contact answers to the questionnaire questions submitted during the assessment. Issue Responses (A) are tracked on issue records. Email Responses (B) are not a VRM response type. Task Responses (C) relate to task completions, not assessment question answers.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the SIG Lite?

options.text: The SIG Lite is a company specific questionnaire
The SIG Lite is a ServiceNow developed questionnaire
The SIG Lite assesses basic levels of due diligence and provides a broad but high-level understanding about internal security controls
The SIG Lite assesses service providers that store or manage highly sensitive or regulated information

questions.explanation: The SIG Lite assesses basic levels of due diligence and provides a broad but high-level understanding about internal security controls (C). Per the docs: SIG Lite is a lighter version of the Standardized Information Gathering questionnaire. The SIG Full (not Lite) covers highly sensitive/regulated service providers (D). SIG is a Shared Assessments industry standard questionnaire (B is wrong — not ServiceNow developed). It is not company-specific (A).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are true about the Template Designer? (Choose two.)

options.text: Question weight can be set in the Template Designer
Correct answers can be set in the Template Designer
Questions can be mandatory in the Template Designer
Dependencies between questions cannot be set in the Template Designer
Questions cannot be mandatory in the Template Designer

questions.explanation: True statements are: Correct answers can be set in the Template Designer (B) and Questions can be mandatory in the Template Designer (C). The designer allows marking questions as required and setting correct answer definitions for scored questions. Question weights (A) are configured separately. Dependencies CAN be set between questions (D is false — conditional logic is supported). E contradicts C.

questions.stem: Which could have an impact on the vendor’s Risk Assessment rating? (Choose three.)

options.text: Answering one or more questions incorrectly
Reassigning a questionnaire to a contact

questions.explanation: Items that could impact a vendor's Risk Assessment rating are answering questions incorrectly (A), leaving answers blank (B), and omitting documentation (C). Incorrect answers produce lower scores; blank answers contribute zero or unfavorable scores; missing document requests leave scoring gaps. Spelling errors (D) do not affect the calculated score. Reassigning a questionnaire (E) changes the respondent but does not directly impact scoring.

questions.stem: During the Generating Observations phase of the Vendor Risk Assessment, what action might be taken by the Risk Assessor?

options.text: Create issues from the assessment if necessary
Answer questions the vendor forgot to answer

questions.explanation: During the Generating Observations phase, the Risk Assessor creates issues from the assessment if necessary (A). The assessor reviews vendor responses and raises issues for gaps, deficiencies, or policy violations identified in the questionnaire responses. Updating the risk score (B) happens automatically based on assessment closure. Emailing the vendor (C) occurs in prior phases. Answering forgotten questions (D) is the vendor's responsibility.

questions.stem: For each questionnaire template/assessment metric type, how many vendor risk areas can be designated?
questions.explanation: As many vendor risk areas as desired (B) can be designated for each questionnaire template/assessment metric type. Per the docs: templates support adding 'third-party risk areas' to specify applicable risk domains. There is no documented limit restricting the number to one (A) or two (D). Templates can also have zero designated risk areas (C is not correct as the typical configuration includes at least one).

questions.stem: To what type of assessment record can a vendor contact respond?
questions.explanation: A vendor contact can respond to a Vendor Risk Assessment (B). External vendor contacts access the Vendor Portal to complete questionnaires associated with vendor risk assessments sent to their organization. Tiering assessments (A) are internal assessments completed by internal assessors. Customer assessment (C) and External monitoring assessment (D) are not standard VRM assessment types accessible to vendor contacts.

questions.stem: What are individual questions within a questionnaire or document request referred to as?
questions.explanation: Individual questions within a questionnaire or document request are referred to as Metrics (A). Per the docs: 'Metric or Assessment metric: A single question within a questionnaire template.' Categories group metrics; metric types/questionnaire templates contain categories. Ratings (B) are scoring results. Templates (C) are the overall structures. Tiers (D) are vendor classification levels.

questions.stem: In addition to the “Design canvas”, which elements does the Template Designer contain? (Choose three.)

options.text: Header bar which contains tabs that display different view and a menu of various functions
Controls for the supported question data types
Question and Categories tabs that contain question/categories that were added to the Question Bank
Risk criteria to identity conditions and risk areas

questions.explanation: In addition to the design canvas, the Template Designer contains a Header bar with tabs and functions (A), Controls for supported question data types (B), and Question and Categories tabs from the Question Bank (D). Per the docs: the designer has a controls palette for data types, a questions library, and a categories view. FAQ Page/Tour (C) is not a standard designer element. Risk criteria for conditions (E) is configured separately in assessment setup.

questions.stem: In the baseline, what component sends reminder notifications about assessments?

options.text: Events fired by a Business Rule

questions.explanation: In the baseline, reminder notifications about assessments are sent by a Workflow (D). The VRM application includes pre-configured workflows that handle assessment lifecycle automation including reminder notifications at defined intervals before due dates. On-demand triggers (A) require manual action. Business Rule events (B) trigger notifications but the overall reminder orchestration is workflow-driven. Scheduled Jobs (C) handle score collection, not assessment reminders.

questions.stem: Vendor Risk Tasks are saved to which one of the following tables?
questions.explanation: Vendor Risk Tasks are saved to the [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_task] table (D). Per the docs: 'Tasks [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_task]' is explicitly listed in the due diligence data model. The base task table [task] (A) is the parent. planned_task (B) is for project tasks. sn_vendor_risk_task (C) is not the correct table name — the actual table has the sn_vdr_risk_asmt prefix consistent with the VRM scoped application.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to create a new Vendor Risk Issue?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to create a new Vendor Risk Issue is Vendor Risk Assessor [sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_assessor] (A). Per the docs: the TPR assessor role includes permissions to create and manage issues identified during assessments. Vendor Assessment Reviewer (B) has read-only/review access. Vendor Risk Manager (C) has higher-level management access. System Administrator (D) is not the minimum — the assessor role is sufficient.

questions.stem: What are the features of Vendor Risk Issues? (Choose two.)

options.text: Generate audit tasks for the vendor risk team
Can only be seen by the customer’s vendor risk team
Provide vendor direct access to update and respond to Issues
Can be generated on-demand or automatically due to an incorrect answer

questions.explanation: Features of Vendor Risk Issues are providing vendor direct access to update and respond to Issues via the Vendor Portal (C) and being generated on-demand or automatically due to an incorrect answer (D). Issues can be auto-triggered by questionnaire responses that fail criteria or manually created by the assessor. Generating audit tasks (A) is not a VRM issue feature. Issues are visible to vendors in the portal (B is wrong — they are not internal-only).

questions.stem: Vendor Risk Issues are usually created in which stage of an Assessment?
questions.explanation: Vendor Risk Issues are usually created during the Generating Observations stage (B). Per the docs: assessment states include 'Generating observations, Responses received, Finalizing with third party.' During Generating Observations the assessor reviews vendor responses and creates issues for identified gaps. Responses Received (A) is the prior state when responses arrive. Submitted to Vendor (C) and Finalizing with Vendor (D) occur before or after issue creation.

questions.stem: A Vendor Risk Task can be created from which of the following records?
questions.explanation: A Vendor Risk Task can be created from a Vendor Risk Issue, Assessment, or Vendor record (D). Tasks are the work items for remediation and follow-up, traceable back to the issue, the assessment context, or the vendor relationship. Risk (B) and Policy (A/B/C) are not sources for VRM tasks. Option C including Policy is incorrect for standard VRM task creation.

questions.stem: What are some of the purposes of a Vendor Risk Issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Log access-related incidents for the vendor portal
Indicate vendors that need further assessment
Accept risks identified in the assessment

questions.explanation: Purposes of a Vendor Risk Issue are to indicate vendors that need further assessment (B) and to track remediation of compliance gaps (D). Issues flag specific deficiencies requiring attention and serve as remediation tracking records. Logging access incidents (A) is not a VRM issue purpose. Accepting risks (C) is a separate risk acceptance process, not an issue function.

questions.stem: The VRM issue management process is frequently unique to an organization. What two ServiceNow provided building blocks were covered in this course to help with customer needs that might arise during the lifecycle of VRM issues? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two ServiceNow building blocks for VRM issue lifecycle customization are Flow Designer (A) and Workflow Editor (C). Both tools enable organizations to automate and customize issue management processes to fit unique requirements. Service Management (B) and Incident Management (D) are product applications, not automation building blocks covered in VRM course context.

questions.stem: In the Vendor Portal, who can reassign Assessments?
questions.explanation: In the Vendor Portal, the Primary Contact (C) can reassign assessments to other vendor contacts. The Primary Contact has elevated management privileges within the vendor organization's portal access. Regular vendor contacts (B) can view and respond but cannot reassign. Vendor Business Owner (A) and Vendor Manager (D) are not standard Vendor Portal role designations.

questions.stem: A Vendor Risk Assessment that consists of a SIG Lite questionnaire and two document requests are displayed as how many total requests in the Vendor Portal?
questions.explanation: A Vendor Risk Assessment with a SIG Lite questionnaire and two document requests displays as 3 total requests (B) in the Vendor Portal. Each questionnaire and each document request is shown as a separate individual request: 1 (SIG Lite) + 2 (document requests) = 3. Requests are not combined into a single item (D) and are not hidden (C).

questions.stem: When an assessor creates an issue or task from the vendor record, it is grouped with other issues or tasks for what ServiceNow entity?
questions.explanation: When an assessor creates an issue or task from the vendor record, it is grouped with other issues or tasks for that specific Vendor (A). All issues and tasks associated with a vendor are visible and grouped on the vendor's Company record, providing a consolidated view of vendor-specific work items. Grouping by All vendors (B), Assessment (C), or Remediation plan (D) is not how VRM tasks are organized from the vendor record.

questions.stem: Who is able to change the password for the vendor contact? (Choose two.)

options.text: Vendor contact via the Forgot Password link

questions.explanation: The sys_admin (B) and the vendor contact via the Forgot Password link (C) can change the vendor contact password. Per the docs: admins can 'Set Password — Generate a new password and send it to the third-party contact.' Vendor contacts can self-service via Forgot Password. Vendor Contract Relationship Manager (A) and Vendor Risk Reviewer (D) do not have password management permissions for external contacts.

questions.stem:
Which statement accurately describes the visibility and audit history of actions and communications in the Vendor Risk Management application?
							
						















													A.
												

											
											The vendor and assessor interactions are captured in the Vendor Risk Issue record and are only visible from the portal view
										





													B.
												

											
											The Vendor Risk Issues created and the activity and history are lost from the Vendor Assessment Portal when the associated vendor contact changes
										





													C.
												

											
											The Vendor Risk Issues created and the activity and history will remain in the Vendor Assessment Portal even when vendor contacts change
										





													D.
												

											
											The vendor and assessor interactions are captured in the Vendor Risk Issue record and are only visible from the platform view
The assessment page provides an area to import what kind of a completed questionnaire?
questions.explanation: The assessment page provides an area to import a completed SIG (Standardized Information Gathering) questionnaire (C). Per the docs: vendors can upload pre-filled SIG spreadsheets from the Third-party portal. The SIG is the industry-standard third-party risk questionnaire natively supported by VRM. GDPR (A), SOC1 & SOC2 (B), and SOX (D) are compliance frameworks but not importable questionnaire types in the VRM assessment page.

questions.stem: How are Vendor Risk questionnaires and document requests displayed on the Vendor Portal?

options.text: As separate requests and can be assigned to different vendor contacts
As separate requests and can only be assigned to the same vendor contact
As a single assessment assigned to a single vendor contact
As a single assessment assigned to a single engagement contact

questions.explanation: In the Vendor Portal, questionnaires and document requests are displayed as separate requests and can be assigned to different vendor contacts (A). Per the docs: different questionnaires can be assigned to different contacts — 'One set collects information on the third-party organization. The TP contact responds to that questionnaire. The other set collects information on the business unit.' Assigning all to the same contact (B) is optional but not required.

questions.stem: In the Paris release and beyond, the scoped vendor portal (svdp) will be installed by default but can be overridden in which System Property record to use the legacy/traditional vendor portal (vdp)?
questions.explanation: To override the default scoped vendor portal (svdp) to use the legacy portal (vdp), update the sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_portal_endpoint system property (C). This property controls the portal endpoint URL used for vendor access. The scoped prefix variants (B, D) are not the correct property names. sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_portal (A) is not the endpoint configuration property.

questions.stem: Which of these must be true in order for a vendor risk issue to be visible in the Vendor Portal?

options.text: There must be at least one secondary contact for the vendor
The primary vendor contact must have the sn_vdr_issues role
Issues are always visible in the vendor portal
The Visible in vendor portal field must have a value of true

questions.explanation: For a vendor risk issue to be visible in the Vendor Portal, the 'Visible in vendor portal' field must have a value of true (D). This field gives the assessor control over which issues are shared with the vendor. Not all issues are automatically visible (C is wrong). Secondary contacts (A) and special roles (B) are not the controlling factors for portal visibility.

questions.stem: Which GRC records can be related to an Entity? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: GRC records that can be related to an Entity are Entity Types (A), Risks (C), and Controls (E). Entities are the organizational objects (business units, processes) assessed in GRC — they have types classifying them, risks quantifying exposures, and controls addressing those risks. Vendors (B) are entities themselves, not records related to an entity. Policies (D) relate to entities indirectly through citations and controls, not as direct entity relationships.

questions.stem: A vendor is assessed and responds to a question which impacts one of the Controls applied to them. When is the Control Status updated?

options.text: When the Vendor Risk Assessment State is Responses Received
When the Vendor Risk Assessment State is Finalizing with Vendor or Closed
When the Vendor Risk Assessment response is saved
When all Questions in the Vendor Risk Assessment have a response

questions.explanation: The Control Status is updated when the Vendor Risk Assessment state is Finalizing with Vendor or Closed (B). Per the docs: questionnaire responses influence control compliance status — the update occurs when the assessment reaches the finalization stages and responses are processed. Responses Received (A) is too early. Per-response save (C) or all-questions complete (D) are not the trigger points for control status recalculation.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of using both VRM and GRC/IRM?

options.text: Vendor Risk engagements automatically match with Audit engagements
All compliance controls are automatically visible to the vendor risk manage
Primary vendor contacts can then see their overall non compliant risk score
Non compliant controls automatically adjust the risk score for a vendor entity

questions.explanation: The advantage of using both VRM and GRC/IRM is that non-compliant controls automatically adjust the risk score for a vendor entity (D). Per the docs: when questionnaire responses are linked to control objectives, control compliance status influences the entity risk score. VRM engagements don't auto-match audit engagements (A). Controls are not automatically visible to VRM managers (B). Vendor contacts don't see internal risk scores (C).

questions.stem: On which of the following tables can you create vendor risk reports? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Tables for vendor risk reports are Company [core_company] (A), Vendor Risk Assessment [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_assessment] (B), and Vendor Risk Issue [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_issue] (C). Per the docs: these three are the primary VRM data tables. Company stores vendor records with tier/risk ratings; Assessment stores assessment results; Issue stores identified risk gaps. Vendor Contact (D) and Vendor Activity (E) are not primary reporting data sources.

questions.stem: A Vendor Risk Manager needs to run a report displaying Critical Vendors. On which table would this person run a report?
questions.explanation: To report on Critical Vendors, run a report on the Company [core_company] table (A). Vendor records including tier/criticality classification are stored in the Company table. Per the docs: 'Vendors by Risk Rating' reports use the company table. Vendor Risk Issue (B) stores issue records. Vendor Contact (C) stores contact persons. Vendor Risk Assessment (D) stores assessment instances, not vendor-level tier/criticality data.

questions.stem: Key data sources for Vendor Risk reporting include which of the following tables? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Key data sources for Vendor Risk reporting are Vendor Risk Assessment [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_assessment] (A) and Vendor Risk Issue [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_issue] (E). Per the docs: these are the primary operational VRM tables. Questionnaire Templates (B) are configuration records. Vendor Benchmark Scores (C) and Survey Scores (D) are not core VRM reporting tables.
